business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1 Business section.
business_model.claim: Star Group operates one reportable segment: a home heating oil and propane distributor and services provider to residential and commercial customers in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic U.S. regions.
quotes: Star Group, L.P. ("Star" the "Company," "we," "us," or "our") is a home heating oil and propane distributor and services provider with one reportable operating segment that principally provides heating related services to residential and commercial customers.

We are a home heating oil and propane distributor and service provider to residential and commercial customers whose primary use is to heat their homes and buildings in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic U.S. regions.

business_model.claim: Fiscal 2025 revenue was split approximately 63% home heating oil and propane, 18% other petroleum products (mainly diesel and gasoline), and 19% installation and repair of heating and air conditioning equipment and ancillary services.
quotes: During fiscal 2025, total sales were comprised of approximately 63% from home heating oil and propane, 18% from other petroleum products, the majority of which is diesel and gasoline, and 19% from the installation and repair of heating and air conditioning equipment and ancillary services.

business_model.claim: As of September 30, 2025, Star served approximately 406,400 full-service residential and commercial customers and 63,200 delivery-only customers for home heating oil and propane, plus approximately 27,700 motor fuel customers; 96% of the full-service fuel base was residential.
quotes: As of September 30, 2025, we sold home heating oil and propane to approximately 406,400 full service residential and commercial customers and 63,200 customers on a delivery only basis.
We also sell gasoline and diesel fuel to approximately 27,700 customers.
Our full service home heating oil and propane customer base is comprised of 96% residential customers and 4% commercial customers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors and Business sections.
business_model.claim: Star's gross profit is a per-gallon margin over wholesale supply cost; the business is explicitly described as 'margin-based,' meaning profitability is sensitive to the spread between retail selling price and wholesale product cost.
quotes: Our business is a "margin-based" business in which gross profit depends on the excess of sales prices per gallon over supply costs per gallon.
It is common practice in our business to price our liquid products to customers based on a per gallon margin over wholesale costs.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A Per Gallon Gross Profit Margins section.
business_model.claim: Home heating oil and propane per-gallon gross margin for fiscal 2025 was $1.7022 per gallon, up $0.0222 (1.3%) from $1.6800 in fiscal 2024; motor fuel and other petroleum products gross margin was $0.3559 per gallon.
quotes: home heating oil and propane margins for fiscal 2025 increased by $0.0222 per gallon, or 1.3%, to $1.7022 per gallon, from $1.6800 per gallon during fiscal 2024.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Customers and Pricing section with a five-year table.
business_model.claim: Residential customers choose among three pricing plans—variable (67.7%), ceiling (25.9%), and fixed (6.4%) as of September 30, 2025—determining how much wholesale price risk Star retains versus the customer.
quotes: We offer several pricing alternatives to our residential home heating oil and propane customers. Our "variable" pricing program allows the price to float with the heating oil market and other factors. In addition, we offer price-protected programs, which establish either a "ceiling" or a "fixed price" per gallon that the customer pays over a defined period.

business_model.basis: Stated in both the 10-K Business (Seasonality) and Risk Factors sections.
business_model.claim: Revenue is highly seasonal: approximately 30% of home heating oil and propane volume is sold in fiscal Q1 (October–December) and 50% in fiscal Q2 (January–March), the peak heating season; the company generally earns net income in Q1–Q2 and net losses in Q3–Q4.
quotes: The seasonal nature of our business results in the sale of approximately 30% of our volume of home heating oil and propane in the first fiscal quarter and 50% of our volume in the second fiscal quarter of each fiscal year, the peak heating season.

we generally realize net income in our first and second fiscal quarters and net losses during our third and fourth fiscal quarters and we expect that the negative impact of seasonality on our third and fourth fiscal quarter operating results will continue.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 8-K earnings release and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Weather (heating degree days) is a primary volume driver: fiscal Q3 2026 temperatures were 15.9% colder year-over-year yet volume still fell 9.4% because the colder-degree-day effect was more than offset by net customer attrition and other factors.
quotes: The amount of home heating oil and propane sold during the fiscal 2026 third quarter declined by 3.4 million gallons, or 9.4 percent, to 32.8 million gallons, as the additional volume provided from acquisitions and colder temperatures was more than offset by the impact of net customer attrition and other factors. Temperatures in Star's geographic areas of operation for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were 15.9 percent colder than the three months ended June 30, 2025 but 5.9 percent warmer than normal.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors and MD&A Customer Attrition sections.
business_model.claim: Net customer attrition is a structural headwind: fiscal 2025 net attrition was 4.7% (19,600 accounts lost), with gross losses of 13.5% partially offset by gross gains of 8.8%; losses to natural gas and electricity conversions were 1.3% of the base.
quotes: Net customer attrition is the difference between gross customer losses and customers added through marketing efforts.
For fiscal 2025, the Company lost 19,600 accounts (net), or 4.7%, of its home heating oil and propane customer base.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A Acquisitions section and the 8-K earnings release.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 8-K earnings release and 10-Q MD&A.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors, 10-Q MD&A, and visible in the 10-Q income statement (F2).
business_model.claim: Star does not apply hedge accounting to its commodity derivatives; changes in fair value of derivative instruments are recognized in the statement of operations, creating significant non-cash earnings volatility that can swing results by tens of millions of dollars in a quarter.
quotes: Currently, we have elected not to designate our derivative instruments as hedging instruments under FASB ASC 815-10-05 Derivatives and Hedging, and the change in fair value of the derivative instruments is recognized in our statement of operations.
we experience volatility in earnings as outstanding derivative instruments are marked-to-market and non-cash gains or losses are recorded prior to the sale of the commodity to the customer.

risks.claim: Because the company does not apply hedge accounting to its commodity derivatives, mark-to-market changes flow directly through the income statement, creating significant earnings volatility; in Q3 2026 alone, an $8,019 thousand unfavorable derivative change contributed to the quarterly net loss.
quotes: we have opted out of, and do not follow hedge accounting for our commodity derivative instruments as hedging instruments, as a result, the changes in fair value of the commodity derivative instruments are recognized in our statement of operations.

Therefore, we experience volatility in earnings as outstanding derivative instruments are marked-to-market and non-cash gains and losses are recorded prior to the sale of the commodity to the customer.
